home.hero_title: Segregate waste instantly with AI, not guesswork.
home.hero_sub: EcoSort AI uses an AI vision model to identify what you're holding up to the camera — almost anything, not just a fixed list — and tells you exactly which bin it belongs in: biodegradable, recyclable, non-recyclable, e-waste or hazardous.
home.features_sub: Multi-object detection, classification logic, real disposal guidelines, and a bit of extra polish.
home.f1_text: An AI vision model scans your webcam capture or uploaded photo and identifies every waste item it can find — not limited to a small predefined list.
home.f2_text: Every detected item is sorted into Biodegradable, Recyclable, Non-Recyclable, E-Waste or Hazardous, with clear disposal guidance.
home.f3_text: Built-in text-to-speech reads out disposal instructions the moment an item is identified — hands-free, and available in multiple Indian languages.
home.f4_text: Every correctly segregated item earns points, streaks and badges — gamifying good waste-disposal habits.
home.f5_text: An AI chatbot that remembers your conversation and answers waste-disposal and sustainability questions in your language.
home.f6_text: Deployed as a live website — works from any phone or laptop, anywhere, any time, with no setup needed.
home.cta_text: Point your webcam at a bottle, a banana peel, or an old phone and watch EcoSort AI classify it in real time.

guidelines.title: Segregation Guidelines
guidelines.subtitle: Tap a card to see the full how-to. The colours match the bins the app tells you to use.
guidelines.points_intro: Points you earn per item, by category:

biodegradable.title: Biodegradable Waste
biodegradable.summary: Organic matter that decomposes naturally through biological processes.
guidelines: Collect in a separate green/organic bin, ideally lined with a compostable or paper bag — not plastic.
Keep it dry-ish; excess liquid speeds up foul odour and pest attraction.
Where possible, compost at home or through a municipal composting scheme — it turns into nutrient-rich manure in 30–60 days.
Never mix with plastic, glass or e-waste — even a small amount of contamination ruins an entire compost batch.
Dispose of daily in warm climates to avoid odour and pests.

recyclable.title: Recyclable (Dry) Waste
recyclable.summary: Clean, dry materials — paper, plastic, glass, metal — that can be reprocessed into new products.
guidelines: Rinse containers to remove food residue before disposal — contamination is the #1 reason recyclables end up in landfill.
Flatten cardboard boxes and plastic bottles to save space and ease transport.
Separate by material where your local facility requires it (paper / plastic / glass / metal).
Remove caps and labels if your recycler asks for it (varies by locality).
Never recycle broken glass loose — wrap it and mark it to protect handlers.

non_recyclable.title: Non-Recyclable (Reject) Waste
non_recyclable.summary: Mixed-material, soiled, or low-value items that current recycling streams cannot process.
guidelines: Minimise generation at source — avoid single-use, multi-layered packaging where possible.
Store separately from recyclables and biodegradables so it doesn't contaminate them.
Dispose of through your municipal solid-waste collection; it typically goes to a landfill or waste-to-energy facility.
Never burn this waste — burning plastics/thermocol releases toxic dioxins and furans.

e_waste.title: E-Waste
e_waste.summary: Discarded electrical/electronic devices and accessories — contains valuable recoverable metals as well as toxic substances.
guidelines: NEVER put e-waste in regular household bins — it contains lead, mercury, cadmium and other toxins that leach into soil and groundwater.
Wipe/factory-reset devices to protect your personal data before handing them over.
Hand over to an authorised e-waste recycler or a manufacturer take-back/collection programme.
Many electronics retailers and municipal bodies run periodic e-waste collection drives — look these up locally.
Batteries should ideally be dropped at dedicated battery-collection boxes, not thrown with other e-waste.

hazardous.title: Hazardous Waste
hazardous.summary: Chemically reactive, corrosive, toxic, flammable or infectious waste requiring specialised handling.
guidelines: Never pour down the drain or mix with regular waste — it can contaminate water supplies and injure sanitation workers.
Store in original, labelled, sealed containers away from children and heat sources.
Return expired medicines to a pharmacy take-back scheme where available.
Hand fluorescent bulbs and batteries to specialised collection points — they contain mercury/heavy metals.
Contact your local municipal body for scheduled hazardous-waste pickup or drop-off events.

non_recyclable.label: Non-Recyclable (Reject Waste)

e_waste.label: E-Waste
e_waste.tip: Electronic/electrical items. Contains recoverable metals and toxic components.

hazardous.label: Hazardous Waste
hazardous.tip: Chemically reactive, toxic or flammable waste needing special handling.

ignore.label: Not Waste
ignore.tip: Not a waste item. This project focuses on segregating discarded objects, so people, animals, vehicles and furniture are ignored.
